filter_screen.description: A 3D-to-2D projection surface using a real Camera3D inside a SubViewport. Unlike the ScienceScreen (grid data), the FilterScreen projects the live 3D scene onto a flat monitor — teaching projection itself as a primitive. Filter modes: normal, wireframe, depth, normals, silhouette, grid overlay. Points foreshorten, lines lose depth, triangles change area based on viewing angle.

science_screen.description: A large display that projects nearby 3D artifacts into simplified 2D abstractions. The screen keeps the structure of the source object but changes its representational state, turning embodied experience into diagram. That makes it a useful bridge between moving through a form and reasoning about it. It stages projection as a transformation with both gains and losses.
science_screen.name: Science Screen
science_screen.qfep_connection: Transformation here is projection: a 3D state is re-expressed in 2D while preserving selected structural relations. It shows how representation changes without becoming arbitrary.
science_screen.capacity: COMPARE a 3D artifact with its 2D abstraction and see what structure survives projection.
interactions: bring a grid-aware artifact near the screen
compare the embodied 3D object with its flat rendering
read algorithm labels and cell statistics on the display
use the screen to reflect on what projection keeps and discards
